subject: opposed to zone change Item #5, Item #6 - 200 N Lakeshore Dr.
comment: Brandon, Thank you for your call today. Here are some of the concerns I have with the proposed zone change. For the record I live on 3000 West, just East of the proposed changes. * The proposed lot size .18 is significantly smaller than the existing lot size on 3000 West of .27 (avg). This will result in smaller homes and put downward pressure on the value of existing homes. * The subdivision just south of the proposed development has an average lot size of .67, again negatively affecting the value of existing homes, with a much smaller lot size. * People say that the land owner has a right to develop his property but I say the existing homeowners also have a right to protect their investment. They purchased their land and built homes based on existing zoning rules and any changes that will affect their investments must be considered. * Even if you change the zoning it should be consistent with the surrounding neighborhoods. Look at the subdivisions located to the East and they are zoned R1.10 not the smaller R1.8. * By putting larger lots you will have fewer homes and putting less pressure on the infrastructure, by using less water, gas, electricity, smaller sewer flows, etc. * While I would prefer not to have any development take place, I strongly suggest that at a minimum, you make the zoning R1.10 not the smaller R1.8. Respectfully Dean Griffin Provo, Ut 84601

subject: Mixed housing
comment: This is Boyd and Sandy Brady, we would like to express our concerns on the plans for mixed housing requirements for southwest Provo. From someone who lives on Center street. We will try and make this short. There are more developments that are being proposed, the land West of Tom Halliday and East of Benjamin Allen, where approx 72 homes may be built. We spoke to Steve Gleason, the Airport manager about the expansion of the airport, we asked how many commercial airlines they are planning on, he said as many as they can get. Right now when a jet lands the line of cars going up center street is steady and that's only one airline.There is also Duncan Aviation that employs hundreds. With traffic as is, we have a hard time backing out of our driveway, Boyd has to drive out forward in the morings due to the employees going to work. We also have concerns about our educational system. What about the schools if there are smaller houses/apartments/townhouses, that means small families with young children. The elementary school is full, I don't see where land is to build another school. The cars get backed up onto Lakeshore drive over a block when trying to turn onto center street when the high school gets out. This intersection has seen multiple accidents. Most of these neighborhoods that are built with higher density housing attract a large number of investors. I have seen this happen with the Rivers in our neighborhood. Our son, who was the president of his HOA Condo complex, said that he knew of at least one person from California who had bought three condos and converted them to rentals. Almost 60% of the complex are now rentals. I personally know of several individuals that have bought townhouses for income property. I know that will happen here. The dynamic of the neighborhood will change drastically, look at Stubbs Ave in Provo. They don't give enough parking for these higher density housing projects, just go up Geneva road into Orem where they have built similar properties, they are parking their cars on Geneva road. Good people will move out. Please I beg you not to make mixed housing in this beautiful west end of Provo. Thank you for taking the time to read this. Boyd and Sandy Brady
